The search didn't turn up anything about "vrslow" in connection with ENLIL. None of the results use the term, so I can't say what it refers to.

The results do cover ENLIL in general. It is a 3D magnetohydrodynamic model of the inner heliosphere, developed by Dusan Odstrcil, that simulates the background solar wind and the interplanetary propagation of coronal mass ejections. It is coupled to the WSA coronal model, which supplies the inner boundary conditions. One paper describes that coupling as a 3D magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) code (ENLIL) that propagates the wind (and any CMEs present in the wind) out to Earth and beyond.

If "vrslow" is a specific variable name, parameter, or file field from an ENLIL output or documentation, a search with the surrounding context (for example, the file or product it appears in) would be more likely to find its meaning.

UA = "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/124.0 Safari/537.36"
listing, outdir = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]

idx = {x["file"]: x for x in json.load(open(listing))["files"]}
os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
for n in names:
    x = idx[n]
    exp = int(x["size"] or 0)
    dst = os.path.join(outdir, n.replace("/", "__"))
    if os.path.exists(dst) and os.path.getsize(dst) == exp and exp > 0:
        print("have", n, exp, flush=True)
        continue
    ok = False
    for k in range(12):
        try:
            req = urllib.request.Request(x["link"], headers={"User-Agent": UA})
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=600) as r, open(dst + ".part", "wb") as f:
                while True:
                    b = r.read(1 << 20)
                    if not b:
                        break
                    f.write(b)
            got = os.path.getsize(dst + ".part")
            if (exp and got == exp) or (not exp and got > 2000):
                os.replace(dst + ".part", dst)
                ok = True
                break
            print("size mismatch", n, got, exp, flush=True)
        except Exception as e:
            print("err", n, repr(e), flush=True)
        time.sleep(5 + random.random() * 15)
    print("ok" if ok else "FAILED", n, exp, flush=True)
